text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-Norwegian electricity producers will post record profits in 1996 following high power prices throughout the year. During 1996 some producers were able to charge double 1995 levels.
-Bank managers won the highest salary increases in the management sector in last year's wage settlements. On average wages rose by 4.25 percent in 1996, up from 3.0 percent in 1995.

-Communications Minister Sissel Roenbeck says there are no current plans to list state-owned telecommunications company, Telenor, on the Oslo Stock Exchange. On Tuesday, newspapers wrote that Telenor manager Tormod Hermansen suggested privatisation of the company.
-Share prices in three gold mining companies listed on the Oslo bourse have risen sharply. In the last two days stocks in Ecuanor, Mindex and Kenor have increased by around 15 percent.

-Analyst Wike Groenenberg at Salomon Brothers in London says the Norwegian crown will rise by six to seven percent against the European Currency Unit index. Under no circumstances does she expect the crown to fall back to 1992 levels.
